items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: I think Chris Kelly was the best with that.

ctx.x: Who was good with a plunge? You're asking who was good with a plunge. Yeah. Yeah.

Well, I'd like to know who used to use the plunge of the boys. Who? Plunger. Who the best trumpet? No. Plunger. Plunger. You know that? Plunger you use with your trumpet? Oh. Let me see. Who got, who got. Oh. I see. So many of them used to do that. I think Chris Kelly was the best with that. Yeah, me too, yeah. And Feli Boo Boo too, you know. Yeah. Used to take some time of glass, a cup, you know. Yeah. Like that, you know. Sometimes used to take your hand, you know. And then that was a good jazz trombone player.…
Yeah. And Feli Boo Boo, you know. Yeah. I think it was Ducey was the jazz trombone.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Before I left here, Bobby was playing with Chris Kelly.

ctx.x: Did you know who Bobby played with first? So they used to arrange for Celestine. Who did Bobby play with? Did you know who Bobby played with?
Bobby? Maybe I learned about this guy's question about a man. Before I left here, Bobby was playing with Chris Kelly.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: He worked me out. He killed me from D to D to D. I didn't make a mistake.

ctx.x: Let's see. Ask him did he play with Chris Kelly before he went to Mexico or after? He said did you play with Chris Kelly before you went to Mexico or after? Oh, long before I went to Mexico. He was a good musician too. He was a good musician too. I asked Chris Kelly to tie you out before he took you in his band.

He worked me out. He killed me from D to D to D. I didn't make a mistake. He told me to say why he got it. Ask him what tune that was. He said what tune was that? It was some wall. I can't think of it.
How much power to build this bamboo

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: No, Chris played most with a plunger.

ctx.x: How did it sound? It sounded good.

Do-do-do-do-dee, bo-do-do-dee, you know what I mean, Paul. Like that, all that kind of stuff. You could do that. Would Chris run those chords? No, Chris played most with a plunger. Yeah. And he played- He played straight along, but he played with a plunger.
Yeah. He'd play ordinary chords, just fifths and ordinary seventh blues chords and stuff like that, but not much money.
